deferred_harness: Each case uses a new extension page, drains automatic initialization, then constructs the packaged CustomWebXRPolyfill. The harness holds its configuration pending, mutates caller options, and dispatches webxr-device-init with the repository profile definition. This uses actual EmulatedXRDevice and DOM Overlay presentation, not fake sessions/devices. Startup no-gesture assertions use the page classic script and the stored profile before controlled initialization.
coverage: Both methods: single mode conversion, string hint, convertible objects, missing/invalid/Symbol modes, rejected Promises and original exceptions; mode conversion precedes options.

Omitted/undefined/null/empty/function dictionaries, primitive failures, explicit undefined absence, inherited/nonenumerable members, ordered single reads without caller enumeration or unknown property reads; null dictionaries do not consult Object.prototype.

Sets, generators and per-element DOMString conversion; invalid sequence inputs/results, Symbols and original iterator/getter/conversion exceptions; one-shot unknown-required rejection, optional omission and viewer/local defaults.

Depth nested ordering, required sequences and valid/invalid enums even without descriptor, depth-type request conversion, boolean/default behavior, CPU preference retention across delayed init, selected unsigned-short format; existing format/depth tests retained.

Nullable overlay, missing/invalid root brands, genuine foreign-realm Element conversion, original-root selection despite mutation; opt-in AR preview, live eligibility checks, required rejection/optional omission and restoration on presentation failure/end.

Conversion before activation and active/pending immersive checks, no presentation resources on conversion failure, activation-free ordinary inline, inline-stereo exception, explicit inline and immersive activation requirements.

Immediate list mutation and configuration delayed across tasks, one-shot feature/depth iterables, overlapping pending/active sessions, recovery after conversion/negotiation/presentation failure and end; failed overlaps preserve active sessions.
Enabled-feature reporting and actual viewer-pose frames after normal and deferred creation; full existing extension bridge, input, sensing, render-state, bounded-floor, Three.js and overlay suite.

wpt_reconciliation.original_assumption: The pinned WPT uses assert_throws_js(TypeError) and expects a synchronous exception from requestSession() without a mode.
wpt_reconciliation.corrected_expectation: The operation returns a Promise rejected with TypeError. Conversion errors retain their original rejection reason.
wpt_reconciliation.primary_reference: Pinned WebIDL es-operations algorithm: exceptions for operations with a Promise return type are returned via Promise.reject.
wpt_reconciliation.rationale: Apply the pinned normative operation binding while preserving the missing-mode error requirement. This discrepancy was already identified in Issue #25; no Issue requirement was weakened or changed.
wpt_reconciliation.adaptation: Equivalent missing-mode, unknown-required, optional-feature and no-gesture assertions in the existing browser harness use real extension sessions and classic-script / Playwright activation instead of upstream fake-device/activation infrastructure.

skips_and_limits: Optional additional upstream WPT files and npm run test:wpt were not executed. Focused applicable assertions were adapted into test:browser.
No Firefox, physical headset/phone, test:samples or native permission/opaque-resource validation was performed for this bounded task.

Depth remains virtual CPU depth with existing formats and defaults. Converted depthTypeRequest may be ignored; matchDepthView=false permits the simulator to continue returning current view-aligned depth.
DOM Overlay retains opt-in original-root preview eligibility and presentation limitations; no native arbitrary-root certification.
Existing Three.js 0.186.1 depth-disabled DepthTexture client error is caught and checked as initialization only, not successful rendering. Depth-enabled paths render successfully.
Broader core/WebIDL, render-state identity and other unfinished inventory modules remain outside Issue #25.

pr_handoff.title: Snapshot WebXR session-request arguments before negotiation (#25)
pr_handoff.problem: XRSystem reread mutable dictionaries after awaiting configuration and consumed one-shot iterables during activation analysis, allowing required features or selected depth formats to change.
pr_handoff.result: Convert mode once in both methods, then convert recognized XRSessionInit dictionaries, iterable elements, depth enums/defaults and Element root once. Activation, negotiation and session initialization reuse converted values, retaining existing activation, immersive ownership and preview lifecycle behavior.
pr_handoff.validation: npm run build and npm run test:browser pass on Chromium 156.0.8078.4. Final focused conversion checks: 351 per immersive combination (each includes inline); deferred initialization: five combinations, 57 assertions total plus 40 startup assertions. Full existing browser suite also passes. Initial harness context-lifecycle failure was fixed.
pr_handoff.specifications: Pinned Device CRD 2026-06-09, WebIDL 622910c, Depth WD 2026-08-25 and DOM Overlay WD 2024-09-24. See specifications and wpt_reconciliation above for links and the missing-mode WPT discrepancy.
pr_handoff.publication: No push, PR creation, merge, Issue edit or comment performed. A downstream publisher should include this scope, execution evidence and WPT reconciliation in the implementation PR. No Issue acceptance correction was required.
